safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports feeling hot/cold and sweaty, but has had no fevers.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures hot/cold sweats but does not document 'no fevers' (only notes no measured temperature).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document “no fevers” (while noting hot/cold sweats and no measured temperature) can bias later clinicians toward assuming true fever and potentially overestimate infection severity, but it is unlikely by itself to change management materially. The core symptom (sweats/rigors) is still captured, and the absence of an actual temperature reading limits the clinical weight of the statement either way.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting “no unwell contacts” has limited clinical impact in a routine viral/URI presentation, particularly when key symptoms and negatives (no nausea/vomiting, no abdominal pain) are documented. This is mainly epidemiologic context and rarely drives immediate treatment decisions in this scenario.
